extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and KIPO examiners (Republic of Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for converted applications and for claiming priority under international treaties (Paris Convention/TRIPS) when filing patent/utility model/design applications in the Republic of Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may grant patent after notice of inadmissible conversion if no ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though a converted application cannot be accepted retroactively, it is possible for the examiner to decide to grant a patent after service of notice for inadmissible conversion if there is no ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rejection where converted application contains invention not described in original (post-2006 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a converted application was filed for an invention not described in the original application (original filed on or after Oct 1, 2006), the examiner shall notify the applicant of the ground for rejection; if the applicant cannot address the ground even with written arguments or amendments, the examiner shall decide to reject the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment period for converted applications (retroactive counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed for amendments to the specification or drawings of a converted application is within the period prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 47(1) of the Patent Act, retroactively counted from the filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a converted application fulfills procedural and substantive requirements, it is regarded as an ordinary application and examined on amendments using the original specification/drawings of the converted application as the baseline. Newly added matter after filing is examined under the prohibition on addition of new subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on addition of new subject matter to converted application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention not contained in the original specification of the converted application is newly added through amendments after filing, the examiner shall examine the application according to the requirements prohibiting addition of new subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This also applies when adding an invention described in the specification/drawings of the original application but not described in the converted application's original specification/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application may be filed from a divisional application but not from multiple originals
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can file a converted application by taking a divisional application as the original application. A converted application shall not be filed based on multiple original applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion shall not be deemed legitimate if division and conversion are carried out in a single patent procedure (e.g., converting part of a patent application to a utility model registration in the same single procedure). To convert a part to another type, the applicant should file a divisional first and then a converted application based on that divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of converted application during reexamination/appeal if formalities legitimate; original deemed withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a converted application along with a request for reexamination regarding a rejected application or an appeal against a rejection, the examiner shall accept the converted application if the procedure is legitimate in formalities. If a request for examination is made for the converted application, the examiner shall conduct the examination. For reexamination or appeal, the examiner shall carry out respective procedures with the original application deemed withdrawn under Article 53(4) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application filed while original was pending but returned: filing date is actual converted filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original application was pending before KIPO at the time of filing a converted application, but was returned after conversion, the examiner shall examine the converted application based on the date it was actually filed, not giving the original's filing date retroactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the converted application cannot take the retroactive filing date and has grounds for rejection, the examiner shall notify the applicant of both the reason it cannot take the retroactive date and the grounds for rejection. In absence of rejection grounds, the examiner shall notify why retroactive date cannot be taken (via On-nara EDMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing converted applications after certain time from certified copy of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If thirty days have elapsed from the date when an applicant received a certified copy of the initial decision to reject, the applicant shall not file a converted application if the decision to reject was cancelled through reexamination or a trial decision or if thirty days have not elapsed from the date when a certified copy of the decision to reject was delivered again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of the decision to reject through reexamination does not necessarily nullify the fact that a certified copy of the initial decision to reject was delivered for the first time; therefore conversion may still be disallowed within the thirty-day rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority under treaty — who may claim priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A person eligible for making a priority claim under the treaty is a national of a contracting state of the treaty or a national of a non-contracting state who has a domicile or a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in a contracting state. When multiple applicants, at least one applicant must meet this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting states include members of the Paris Convention and WTO. This includes filings to certain regional offices (EPO, EAPO, OAPI, ARIPO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim only after first application filed in contracting state
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim can be made only after an application was filed in a contracting state of the treaty (the country where it was first filed). If the inventor granted the right to file to another person, the inventor cannot make the priority claim for that first application, although others may file without priority in other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/succession of right to file subsequent applications claiming priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to make any subsequent filing in other treaty countries can be transferred to successors. The successor must be a national of a contracting state both at the time of filing the first application and at the time of filing the subsequent application, although the nationality need not be continuous between filings in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority can be transferred between nationals of contracting/non-contracting states under certain conditions and remain effective if requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing application claiming priority (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to claim priority under the treaty shall file a patent application within one year from the filing date of the first application which forms the basis of the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is reflected in Article 54(2) and specific time calculations follow Paris Convention rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific time periods: one year (patent/utility model) and six months (design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year from the filing date of the first application if priority claim is based on a patent application or utility model registration; within six months if based on a design registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time period is calculated from the day after the filing date of the first application in accordance with Article 4C(2) of the Paris Convention. If the last day falls on an official holiday/closed day, filing may be done the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content in the Korean application to claim priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to claim priority shall state in the patent application the intention to claim priority, the name of the state in which the first application was filed, and the filing date of the first application. The first application number should also be indicated (Article 4D(5) Paris Convention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related payments must be made when claiming priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required to substantiate priority and submission deadline (1 year 4 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who claimed priority must submit to the Commissioner of KIPO documents specified (e.g., certified copies of the first application's specification and drawings or prescribed written statements) within one year and four months from the earliest priority date (or in designated countries the application number may suffice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required evidential documents within the period voids the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined procedures and replacement by application numbers (DAS/EPO/Japan/USPTO conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain countries (e.g., Japan, EPC signatories, WIPO DAS participants), streamlined procedures allow submission of application numbers to replace full evidentiary documents. Whether a filing country qualifies for streamlined procedures is determined by the Korean filing date and other conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only EPO filings can replace evidential documents for EPC signatories. For USPTO, KIPO needs an authorization form (PTO/SB/39) for access. For DAS countries, KIPO must be able to retrieve documents from DAS using application numbers and requests for DAS access must be made in advance in the country of first filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: When multiple priorities include streamlined and non-streamlined countries
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple priority claims are based on both streamlined-procedure countries and non-streamlined countries, only the evidential documents for the streamlined-country application can be replaced by application numbers; documents for non-streamlined countries must follow regular procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may request Korean translation of evidential documents; two-month period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner (as Commissioner of KIPO) requires submission of a Korean translation of the evidential documents to determine patentability (e.g., where prior art may exist between priority date and filing date), the applicant must submit the Korean translation within the designated period of two months, extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is not submitted within the period, the examiner can invalidate the proceedings for the concerned priority claim. Translations are reference materials; amendments to translations are permitted even if they substantially change contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive requirement — acceptable types of first application
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application forming the basis for priority must be one of: a patent application, an application for utility model registration, design registration, or an inventor’s certificate. Design or service mark applications are not recognized bases for patent priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Paris Convention doesn't specify type, practice permits these types per Articles 4E and 4I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive requirement — first application must be regular
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application filed in one of the treaty countries shall be regular; the relevant law of the country determines regularity. Whether the first application remains pending does not affect the priority claim — withdrawal, abandonment, invalidation, or rejection does not negate the priority effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the first application cannot yield a patent in its country, priority claim remains effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earliest application rule (first application must be earliest or recognized as earliest)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application must be the earliest application or one recognized as the earliest-filed application. If a later-filed application already exists for the same invention and displaces an earlier claimed first application, priority cannot be claimed from the non-earliest filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earliest application was filed in a country where priority claim cannot be made, that earliest application is not included in the definition of earliest application for priority purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions under Article 4C for a subsequent application to be recognized as the earliest
rubrics_metrics.description: A subsequent application can be deemed the earliest application if: (1) filed for the same invention in the same country as the previous first application; (2) the previous first application was withdrawn/abandoned/rejected before the subsequent filing; (3) the previous first application was not published; (4) no rights became effective because of the previous first application; (5) the previous first application did not serve as a basis for a priority claim in same/different countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of legitimate priority claim — filing date equivalence for same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim under the Treaty is legitimate, the same invention as described in the first application retains the same filing date as the filing date of the first application for purposes of Articles 29 and 36 of the Patent Act. Inventions excluded from the first application do not take that filing date even if priority claim is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: For certain provisions (e.g., disclosure exception Article 30), failing to file within 12 months after disclosure may cost novelty/inventive step even if priority was filed within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/addition of priority claims period (one year and four months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed for amendment or addition of a priority claim is within one year and four months from the earliest priority date. Designated time for multiple priority claims with Domestic Priority is the same. Addition/withdrawal affects earliest priority date calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 54(7) restricts who may amend/add: the applicant must have made a priority claim at filing and at least one priority claim must meet the one-year requirement. If priority claim fails Article 54(1) and (2) requirements, it is deemed to have uncorrectable errors and amendments/additions are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendment/addition of priority claims is prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment or addition of priority claims is not allowed if the priority claim has been withdrawn or invalidated, the application claiming priority has been invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned, a final decision to grant/reject is conclusive, or all priority claims have been withdrawn (except adding a claim on the same day as complete withdrawal is permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to grant is final when a certified copy of the decision to grant is served; rejection becomes final when thirty days have elapsed from certified copy of rejection being served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawals and clerical corrections allowed within one year and four months
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, withdrawal of all priority claims, withdrawal of part of priority claims in multiple claims, correction of clerical errors in priority indications, and addition of priority claims are permitted. Withdrawal/addition may be made via amendment without separate submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the period, only clerical corrections to priority indications are allowed; changing/specifying/adding the first application is not allowed (except withdrawals remain allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination flow — formalities first, then substantive examination based on priority date if no deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an application claiming priority or a written amendment is submitted, the examiner shall examine the formalities of the priority claim. Unless deficiency is found, the examiner shall carry out substantive examination. If substantive prior art search finds no prior art between the first application's filing date and the claiming application's filing date, the examiner shall examine patentability based on the first application's filing date; where prior art exists, examiner shall examine whether the invention was described in the first application and may request further evidential documents/translations.
